statement: Let n = len(nums), and for any list xs and integer v let freq(xs, v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = v. The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and: (1) len(r) = n; (2) for every integer v, freq(r, v) = freq(nums, v); (3) for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, either freq(nums, r[i]) < freq(nums, r[j]), or freq(nums, r[i]) = freq(nums, r[j]) and r[i] >= r[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r; no failure (overflow, out-of-bounds access, panic, or other failure) occurs for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, freq(r, v) = freq(nums, v), where freq(xs, v) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = v. Equivalently, r is a permutation (multiset rearrangement) of nums.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), freq(nums, r[i]) <= freq(nums, r[j]), where freq(nums, v) is the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), if freq(nums, r[i]) = freq(nums, r[j]), then r[i] >= r[j], where freq(nums, v) is the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v and all indices i, j, k with 0 <= i < j < k < len(r), if r[i] = v and r[k] = v, then r[j] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) >= 1. Let f0 = freq(nums, r[0]), where freq(nums, v) is the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v. Then for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), f0 <= freq(nums, r[j]); and for every j with 0 <= j < len(r) and freq(nums, r[j]) = f0, r[0] >= r[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), min(nums) <= r[j] <= max(nums), where min(nums) is the minimum of nums[i] over 0 <= i < len(nums) and max(nums) is the maximum of nums[i] over 0 <= i < len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of integers v and w that both occur in nums and satisfy freq(nums, v) < freq(nums, w), every occurrence of v in r precedes every occurrence of w in r; that is, for all i and j with 0 <= i < len(r), 0 <= j < len(r), if r[i] = v and r[j] = w, then i < j. Here freq(nums, x) is the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = x.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.
